title: fix(app-shell): write a `conditional` rule’s guard as `when`, the key the spec accepts
body:
Part of #9802

`ObjectValidationsPanel` built a `conditional` rule's guard under the key `condition`, and its shared CEL editor read and wrote that same key — while the spec spells that shape's guard `when` and refuses `condition` **by name**. The same file's docblock promises its skeletons never 422. So the one authoring path whose stated purpose is a save-safe draft produced a refused one.

This is a pull-back to a contract that already exists. Nothing in `@objectstack/spec` was touched.

## The refusal, re-measured at source

The card's whole premise is "the spec refuses this key", so it was re-taken here rather than trusted — against the `@objectstack/spec` this repo resolves (**17.4.0**, resolved from `packages/app-shell`), with a control in the same command, one key changed:

| leg | schema | result |
|---|---|---|
| skeleton as shipped, guard `condition` | `ConditionalValidationSchema` | **refused** — `unrecognized_keys`, keys `condition` |
| same object, guard `when` (control) | `ConditionalValidationSchema` | **accepted** |
| both, again | `ValidationRuleSchema` | refused / accepted |
| both, wrapped in a draft | `ObjectSchema` `validations` index 0 | refused / accepted |

The refusal message is itself explicit: *"Unrecognized key(s) on this conditional validation rule: `condition`. Did you mean `condition` to `when`?"*

**It is not an alias.** A rule carrying `when` **and** `condition` together is still refused, with `unrecognized_keys` on `condition`. So no migration door exists to preserve, and no read-side alias was added.

**And it is not a blanket rename** — this is the trap. The inverse control fires in the same run: `ScriptValidationSchema` **accepts** `condition` and **refuses** `when`. Two spellings are live at once. Running every skeleton the panel emits through the spec showed exactly one broken: `script`, `cross_field`, `state_machine`, `format` and `json_schema` all parse; only `conditional` fails.

## Every site naming the guard key

The card named two places. There are **six functional sites**, and the two it did not name are in `changeType`:

| site | before | disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `makeSkeleton` `script` | `condition` | **correct, untouched** |
| `makeSkeleton` `cross_field` | `condition` | **correct, untouched** |
| `makeSkeleton` `conditional` | `condition` | now `when` |
| `makeSkeleton` nested `then` (a `script` rule) | `condition` | **correct, untouched** |
| shared editor read | `expressionSource(rule.condition)` | keyed per rule |
| shared editor write | `patch` of `condition` | keyed per rule |
| `changeType` read of the old rule | `expressionSource(cur.condition)` | reads the OLD type's key |
| `changeType` write to the new rule | `next.condition` | writes the NEW type's key |

One `conditionField` element serves `script`, `cross_field` **and** `conditional`, so the key is now resolved per rule through a `guardKey` helper rather than baked in. Changing only the skeleton would have left the editor unable to load the rule it had just written.

## What made the "never 422s" promise false with nothing going red

Measured, and the answer is that **nothing ever checked it**:

- `makeSkeleton` is module-private — named in exactly one file in the tree, its own, and exported nowhere.
- Neither existing panel suite imports `@objectstack/spec` or calls any parser (control: both import `vitest`, with 8 and 18 `expect(` calls).
- The `conditional` type is exercised by **zero** existing panel assertions (control: the other five types appear 9 times across the same two files).
- The assertions that do cover skeletons match the emitted object against the panel's own idea of the key. **A producer checked against itself stays green however it spells things.**

This is Commandment 9 exactly: the docblock stated a fact about a foreign schema, derived once and re-derived never.

**Measured proof rather than argument:** under each of the three ablations below, the pre-existing suite stayed **green — 9 passed, every time**, including the mutation that restores the original defect verbatim.

## Ablations

Each: mutate, prove it landed by blob hash, run, restore, prove the restore by hash equality **and** an empty `git diff HEAD`. Trapped on EXIT/INT/TERM with absolute paths.

| ablation | `whenKeyPin` | pre-existing suite |
|---|---|---|
| conditional skeleton back to `condition` | **red** — 3 failed / 8 passed | green (9 passed) |
| `guardKey` always `condition` (the pre-fix editor) | **red** — 3 failed / 8 passed | green (9 passed) |
| `guardKey` always `when` (blanket rename) | **red** — 1 failed, then 2 after strengthening | green (9 passed) |

The third started as a **green that was a finding**: a blanket rename to `when` cost only one assertion, because only the conditional half of the shared editor was pinned. A symmetric script-side round-trip pin was added; that ablation now fails two.

Every restore verified: hash equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty, tree clean.

## The pin

`whenKeyPin` does not assert source text — that is how the defect survived. It drives the real panel and runs what it emits through the spec's own `ValidationRuleSchema` and `ObjectSchema`, the same parse the draft save applies, for **every** rule type the New menu offers. A skeleton that would 422 fails the suite.

## Sweep

- Tests naming the changed file, tree-wide: the two existing panel suites (control: the sibling `ObjectActionsPanel` probe returned its own distinct set in the same run). All run here.
- The whole `studio-design` directory: **58 files / 340 tests pass**.
- Tree-wide for the string being changed, not the file path: every other consumer already spells it `when` — the types package's own docblocks, the validation preview, the draft-level lint from objectui#9497, the core engine, and the parity pin in `packages/types` that asserts `when` / `then` / `otherwise` and not `condition`. **This panel was the last producer disagreeing with the tree.**

## Verification

| check | verdict |
|---|---|
| pin + both existing panel suites | `VERDICT command-exit 0` — 3 files, 26 tests passed |
| `studio-design` directory | 58 files / 340 tests passed |
| app-shell `type-check` | `VERDICT command-exit 0` — 0 error lines |
| eslint, changed files | exit 0, 0 errors |
| changeset presence / claims / no-major | exit 0 |
| vi-mock-shape, test-path-roots, control-bytes, new-line-citations | exit 0 |
| governed-surface guard | NOT GOVERNED — ordinary review route |

Union re-run after the final commit, at `e335cbc86`.

An earlier app-shell `type-check` exit 2 was a **prerequisite failure, not a red gate** — every error was `TS2307: Cannot find module` for workspace packages whose `dist` had never been built. After building the 28-package dependency closure it reported the three real errors, all in the new test, all since fixed.

ESLint narrowing is declared, with its evidence: the population comes from eslint's own resolved config (119 rules for the test file), the file count from `--format json` (2), and type-aware linting is **not** enabled in the flat config — so this diff cannot move the verdict of any file it does not touch. The repo-wide scan remains CI's. One pre-existing warning stands in `JsonField`'s re-sync effect, code this diff never touches.

## Pending-changeset sweep

One pending changeset names this file by symbol: `8167-conditionbuilder-mount-scope.md`, frontmatter `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch` — a package-declaring one, so it **does** publish a CHANGELOG line. Its sentence "An object validation rule's `condition` (`ObjectValidationsPanel`) declares `scope=record`" is **narrowed, not falsified**: the mount still declares that scope for all three CEL-bearing types, but the backticked `condition` now names only two of them. ⛔ Not edited here — reported for the seat to decide.

Worth noting: `check:changeset-claims` passes and prints "No pending changeset names a file this change touches" — correct by its own rule, which matches by backticked **file** name, while 8167 names the panel by **symbol**. The manual sweep is the instrument here, not the gate.

## Acceptance notes

Out-of-scope observations, noted and deliberately **not** filed:

- `scripts/__tests__/check-doc-component-types.test.ts` carries cross-file line-address citations in its fixture comments — the form Commandment 11 bans. Pre-existing, in a file this branch does not touch, and AGENTS.md is explicit that these are repaired opportunistically and never swept. The differential gate reports 0 new citations from this branch. **Successor: whoever next edits that fixture list.**
- The spec's own `ConditionalValidation` docblock authors `when` with bare-shorthand predicates, the spelling the server fail-closes on. That is objectstack's published documentation, reached by nothing in objectui — already recorded on the card by the filing lane, and outside this repo entirely. **Successor: an objectstack-side card, if anyone takes it.**

## Closing keyword

**`Part of #9802`, deliberately, rather than a closing keyword.** The guard-key defect is closed and pinned, and all three of the card's "not measured" questions are now answered (the other five skeletons parse; the nested `then` is correct as `condition`; no other rule type disagrees). But the card explicitly left one remedy-shape question open — whether the panel should surface the spec's own suggestion text to the author instead of silently writing the corrected key. This PR does not answer it. The seat can close the card by hand if it judges that remainder immaterial; a closing keyword here would decide it silently at merge.
